objective: DICHOTOMY-3D-20261025-001 found that counting homomorphisms from closed 3-manifold groups is #P-hard exactly for non-abelian groups once homology may grow (Galindo 2026). Ask where the line falls when the first homology is bounded. Metabelian targets reduce to a bounded number of twisted-cohomology computations and should stay polynomial; S4 is the first group whose count sums over exponentially many maps into S3 even with bounded H1. First discriminator: counting homomorphisms from knot groups (H1 = Z) to S4 that send meridians to transpositions, through the alternating diagrams of plane graphs with tripled edges, whose 3-colourings are free. Standalone value: the first solvable target whose colouring counts on knots are #P-hard, and the bounded-homology side of the dichotomy.
status: Complete 2026-10-25: counting with bounded first homology. With bounded homology the hardness line moves up one level: every group with an abelian normal subgroup and nilpotent quotient (all metabelian groups) stays polynomial, while counting homomorphisms from knot groups (H1 = Z) to S4 that send meridians to transpositions is #P-hard. The mechanism: on alternating diagrams of plane graphs with tripled edges the S3 colourings are free vertex potentials and the S4 lifts follow the left-right cycles of the monochromatic subgraph (bicycle law), a twelve-state model equal to the 12-state Potts model at v = 1/2 for subdivided graphs (links, one query) and reaching the planar chromatic polynomial at 12 through knot-keeping gadgets (knots). Closed manifolds with bounded first homology remain open. Next: closed manifolds via surgery (2/3); execution deferred to the owner.
stop_rule: Stop if S4 knot colourings reduce to linear algebra, or if no gadget family keeps the diagram a knot while making the count hard.
title: Counting with bounded first homology
